subject: Latency pattern analysis + proposal for dedicated pilot and contract addendum
messages:
From: Danielle Moore <danielle@finserv.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+reliability@finserv.com, procurement@finserv.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:24:00 -0400
Subject: Persistent latency spikes impacting transaction processing

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the call this morning. I wanted to follow up in writing: over the last three weeks we've observed recurring latency spikes on the Redwood API during our peak window (14:00-16:00 EDT) that correlate with batch settlement jobs. The jumps are intermittent but predictable enough that our ops team is flagging them as a material risk for the upcoming renewal.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood commit to a tighter tail-latency SLO for our account (p50/p95/p99) or provide a documented remediation plan?
- If not, would a transition to Dedicated capacity or a short dedicated pilot be an option to stabilize throughput before we finalize the annual contract?

We're approaching our renewal decision and procurement has requested an addendum that outlines any new uptime/latency commitments and price impact if we upgrade tiers. Happy to share logs if helpful (ops@finserv can send).

Appreciate a quick path forward — this is time-sensitive for our Q4 rollout.

Thanks,
Danielle Moore
Head of Platform Engineering
FinServ Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent latency spikes impacting transaction processing

Hi Danielle —

Thanks for writing this up and for the call earlier. I'm really sorry you're seeing these spikes; we take tail latency very seriously. Short answers up front: yes, we can run a short dedicated pilot targeted at your peak window, and we can draft an addendum with explicit SLO targets for p50/p95/p99 during the pilot period.

Proposed next steps (suggested):
1) We'll run a 30-day Dedicated pilot scoped to your settlement jobs (we'll mirror the peak window and traffic profile).
2) During the pilot, we'll instrument additional tracing and share a daily SLO digest (we'll provide the template).
3) If pilot stabilizes tail latency to agreed targets, we will include a formal addendum to the annual contract with the upgraded SLA and pricing.

I'll coordinate internally for capacity and a quick SRE review. Can you have ops send a compressed log extract (1-2 GB) and a short traffic pattern summary? I'll aim to get a pilot scope and timeline within 48 hours.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding Danielle's note. High priority for renewal: FinServ is asking for clear remediation and an addendum if we can hit tighter tail latencies. Key asks from me:

- Priyom: can your team map what a 30-day dedicated pilot looks like (GPU pool sizing, isolation levels, KV cache warmup plan)? We should include continuous batching tweaks + quantization profile suggestions. Also flag any data residency or infra constraints.
- Monica: commercial — we need a slim addendum template that captures p50/p95/p99 targets, measurement methodology, credits for misses, and pricing for Dedicated vs. Premium SLA. Put a placeholder price delta we can show in a 1:1 with FinServ.

I've attached an initial SLO analysis I pulled from our monitoring (slo-analysis.csv) and a rough draft addendum (draft-addendum.docx) with placeholders. I'll coordinate capacity with infra after Priyom's sizing.

I'll keep Danielle updated; we want to move fast.

Ben
attachments: slo-analysis.csv, draft-addendum.docx
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent latency spikes — can we fast-track a dedicated pilot and SLA addendum?

Ben / Monica —

Quick technical read: the pattern FinServ describes (spikes during scheduled batch settlements) points to cold KV cache behavior combined with synchronous autoscaling boundaries. We can mitigate quickly with a targeted Dedicated pool + the following config during the 30-day pilot:
- Pre-warm KV cache for the settlement job keys 30 minutes before window start.
- Fixed-size worker pool for the 14:00-16:00 window (avoid scale-to-zero behavior).
- Enable continuous batching with a max latency cap of 40ms for foreground requests, and reserved capacity for settlement batches.

I'll need a sample traffic file (ops export) to size GPUs correctly; without it I can only give a range. Assuming your peak QPS ~ 850 and 6-token avg responses for the settlement pipeline, I estimate we need 2 x A6000-equivalent nodes with 1.5x buffer for headroom. If they agree to Dedicated long-term, quantization to q4_0 for these models will reduce cost by ~30% without materially changing tail behavior.

I'll draft a short runbook for the pilot and a measurement plan that defines how we compute p50/p95/p99 and what counts as an incident.

Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
